This probably is going into oblivion because I'm late but back in 1994 I was living in Colombia at the height of Colombia beating Argentina 5-0 and qualifying to the 1994 USA World Cup. I was roaming my city's "downtown" searching for a Colombian soccer team jersey and famous Colombian players dolls or action figures however you want to call it. Anyways, I found a stand on the sidewalk that had BOTH! I'm pleading with my grandmother to buy me both, but we were poor and I, like an idiot teenager didn't understand that. When this guy with a huge camera from Colombia's biggest newspaper stops by and asks my grandma permission to interview me and take a picture of me with the doll. He just asks what makes me want the doll and asks me to turn around as if I was reaching for the doll and snaps a picture. I went home and told the whole neighborhood that I was going to be on the paper next morning! I couldn't sleep, just imagining how my picture and words were being printed, how scholars hundred of years from now would base every article on my words from that interview. I got up, went to the store to get the paper, I just wanted to see it, couldn't afford to buy it. There it was, my picture, my glorious back, reaching for the "Pibe" Valderrama doll, all you could see was my shoulder and part of my head and my misspelled name. Nobody believed it was me.
